name: Timothy
source_summary: A young leader from Lystra, raised in the faith by his mother and grandmother, who became Paul's close protégé and companion in ministry, later pastoring the church at Ephesus and receiving two of Paul's letters.
family_friendly_summary: Timothy grew up in Lystra, and his faith in God was nurtured from childhood by his mother, Eunice, and his grandmother, Lois, both devoted believers. When Paul came through Lystra on a missionary journey, he was impressed by Timothy's reputation and invited him to join his ministry team. Timothy became one of Paul's closest and most trusted companions, traveling with him through many difficult and dangerous situations and even being sent on important assignments to encourage struggling churches. Paul treated Timothy almost like a son, offering him encouragement, correction, and guidance. Paul eventually left Timothy to pastor and lead the church in Ephesus, and Paul wrote him two personal letters, 1 and 2 Timothy, full of practical guidance for leading a church well and staying faithful, even though Timothy was still young.
adult_story: Timothy grew up in Lystra with a Jewish mother, Eunice, and grandmother, Lois, both commended for their "sincere faith," though his father was a Greek, apparently not a believer (Acts 16:1; 2 Timothy 1:5). Well spoken of by believers in Lystra and Iconium, Timothy joined Paul's ministry team, and Paul had him circumcised to avoid unnecessary offense to Jews in the region they were about to travel through, even though Paul elsewhere strongly opposed requiring circumcision of Gentile converts (Acts 16:1-3; compare Galatians 5:2-6). Timothy became one of Paul's most trusted companions, mentioned as co-sender of six of Paul's letters and repeatedly sent on sensitive assignments to trouble churches, including Thessalonica and Corinth (1 Thessalonians 3:1-6; 1 Corinthians 4:17; 16:10). Paul's affection for him is unmistakable, calling him "my true child in the faith" and "my beloved son" (1 Timothy 1:2; 2 Timothy 1:2). Paul left Timothy to lead the church at Ephesus, and 1 and 2 Timothy, two of Paul's "Pastoral Epistles," address him personally with detailed guidance on church leadership, sound doctrine, and personal integrity, including Paul's encouragement not to let anyone look down on him for his youth, but to be an example in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity (1 Timothy 4:12). Paul's second letter to Timothy, written from prison shortly before his execution, is among the most personal and urgent in the New Testament, closing Paul's life with a final charge to his closest protégé.
christ_connections: Paul's charge that Timothy had 'known the sacred writings' from childhood, which 'are able to give you the wisdom that leads to salvation through faith in Christ Jesus' (2 Timothy 3:15), makes Timothy Scripture's clearest picture of a life shaped toward Christ from earliest years rather than a dramatic late conversion.

Paul's fatherly love for Timothy -- calling him 'my true child in the faith' -- mirrors the adoption every believer receives in Christ, brought into God's family not by birth but by grace (Galatians 4:4-7).
devotionals: Timothy’s story teaches us about mentorship; may we look to Jesus, whose grace and truth never fail.
Through Timothy’s experience of youthful ministry, God teaches us to trust His wisdom and follow Jesus faithfully.
